Privacy, in plain language

Your work is
not our content.

PULSE uses an authenticated API to store workspace accounts and activity records. Configure the API and deployment to meet your organization's privacy and data-retention requirements.

Activity timing only. Always.

PULSE is designed to understand when you are active or idle—not what you are doing.

What is tracked

  • Session start, pause, and stop times
  • Active and idle duration, stored separately
  • Your selected project or task label
  • Your Productive, Neutral, or Distracting tag
  • Voluntary mood, stress, and workload ratings

What is never tracked

  • Keystrokes or what you type
  • Screen content, screenshots, or recordings
  • URLs, browsing history, or document names
  • Passwords, personal files, or webcam/microphone data

What managers can see

Managers see only aggregated team averages, participation rates, trends, and risk indicators. Team groups below the organization's configured minimum response count are suppressed. Individual pulse responses and personal activity timelines are not included in manager views.

Where workspace data lives

Account, activity, pulse, report, and billing records are stored in the workspace database and scoped to the authenticated organization. The browser stores only the short-lived access session state and non-sensitive preferences; refresh credentials are held in an HTTP-only cookie. Payment details are collected by the configured billing provider and are not submitted to the PULSE API.

Deployment and retention

Workspace operators are responsible for configuring appropriate access, database security, retention, consent, and privacy-review policies before collecting employee data. PULSE does not collect pulse comments.
